lines: Built with: vite.config.ts, package.json declares @nextcloud/vite-config 2.5.4, vite 7.3.7.
Other delivered libraries: 124, focus-trap 8.2.3, axios 1.18.1, util 0.12.5, micromark 4.0.2, sax 1.6.0, mdast-util-to-hast 13.2.1, and 118 more.
Packages and versions are those the .license files beside the chunks name, since the source maps miss packages through the toolchain defect named here.

Known toolchain defect: vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js 4.0.1 in package-lock.json, where the CSS is injected by JavaScript, puts the code that injects the CSS in front of the chunk without shifting its source map, so the map the bundler combines from it loses sources. Here the map of synaplan_integration-files-init.mjs names 8 of the 44 packages its .license file names, and 4 further chunks show the same.
The app runs as built; only the map is short, so the frameworks and libraries are read from the .license files instead.

Built in a copy with @nextcloud/vite-config 3.0.0-beta.1, vite 8.3.5 (vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js 5.0.3), the map of nl-BE-B_qDxKrI.chunk.mjs names 44 of the 45 packages its .license file names: fixed.
Every delivered file in js carries a source map, so every byte can be charged to the package and the module it came from.
2 packages are imported by their root in src, each delivered in fewer than 8 modules, so a per-module import has nothing to leave out and the specifier decides no bytes here.
